source.title: Virtual Assets Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing

summary: GOLDEN LABEL, hand-drafted against the PDF. FATF red flag indicator report on the misuse of virtual assets, drawn from over one hundred case studies contributed 2017-2020, grouped by transaction size and frequency, transaction patterns, anonymity, sender and recipient profile, source of funds or wealth, and geographical risk. The techniques it describes are mostly crypto-native and absent from the governed library: mixing and tumbling services (Helix), conversion across multiple virtual assets and exchanges, immediate swaps into anonymity-enhanced coins, unregistered peer-to-peer exchange and unlicensed money transmission, unhosted and hardware wallets carried across borders, VASPs relocating to jurisdictions without AML/CFT rules, darknet marketplace exposure (AlphaBay, DeepDotWeb), virtual asset ATMs, crypto-to-plastic card cash-out, shell wallets controlled from one IP address, and forged identity documents to defeat VASP KYC. Conventional typologies carry over: structuring below thresholds, mule accounts recruited by professional launderers or converted from scam victims, funnel-style accumulation wallets, rapid movement through multiple VASPs, layering, and shell companies holding the bank accounts. Sanctions evasion and terrorist financing are named as observed uses but not developed. Thirteen case studies sourced from South Africa, South Korea, the Czech Republic, the Cayman Islands, the United States, Russia, Italy and Finland.

extraction_notes: Golden label. Pages 1-5, 21-24 are cover, contents, acronyms, introduction, conclusion, references and back matter; printed folio is the PDF index minus two for pages 4-22 and absent elsewhere. The whole report is a list of red flags, so the convention that indicators are not typologies was applied as: label a behaviour when the report gives it a heading, a case study or repeated treatment, not a single bullet. CMI010 is the library's only crypto entry and is defined as sanctions evasion; the report names VA sanctions evasion only in passing (p6 trends box, sanctioned IPs p14, sanctioned addresses p17), so it is medium and everything crypto-native is emergent in the crypto family, one label per technique. BA001 is medium because the report itself equates VA structuring with cash structuring and case 13 is genuine sub-USD 10,000 cash importation; the correspondent-banking family is applied to VA flows by analogy the report draws explicitly (p7). BA002 rests on the accumulation-wallet bullet (p10) and the DDW pattern of 40,000 deposits out through 2,700 withdrawals; medium because no case is framed as a funnel account. PAT007 chosen over TBML009 because the shell companies hold bank accounts for laundering, not trade. SAN008 is applied in its general high-risk-jurisdiction sense to the geographic risk section, though the report explicitly declines to name high-risk jurisdictions (p19), so no jurisdiction enters the list on risk grounds. The VASP relocation case (p20, jurisdictions A-D) is labelled separately from SAN008 because the actor moving is the VASP, not the customer. Not labelled: ransomware, gambling and ICO proceeds (bullets only, source-of-funds rather than technique), terrorist financing (named, never developed), PAT005 shared residential address in case 1 (single indicator of a mule ring), BA006 previously inactive account (one line). The Finland investment scam (case 10) is folded into BA003 and the mule actor rather than labelled as a fraud typology, since the report's interest is the laundering leg. Jurisdictions are the eight case-contributing states, on the reading that the case sits where it was investigated and reported; KY and FI are the weakest, since the Cayman case was an attempted theft frozen abroad and the Finnish victims were pensioners, but both cases and their mules ran there. Case 9's Asia, Europe, Africa and Middle East, case 13's Asian exchange and US-bordering jurisdiction, and case 3's onward account in the Czech Republic (already listed) are not resolved further. France appears only as FATF's address. Actors: AlphaBay, Helix and DeepDotWeb are named criminal enterprises with no stated jurisdiction; the Helix operator, DDW owners, bitcoin dealer, and relocating VASP are anonymised and not labelled. FATF, FIUs, LEAs and reporting entities are not actors.
